# F1: Data loading and SQL preparation

*Generated by `python -m forecast.run_f1` from `results/f1_data_report.json`. Do not edit the
numbers by hand.*

## What this step does, in plain words

Walmart's M5 file stores sales "wide": one row per product per store, and one column per day
(1,941 day columns). Forecasting needs it "long": one row per product, store and day. F1 does
that reshaping in SQL (DuckDB), attaches the real date, holidays/events and SNAP food-benefit days
from the calendar, and attaches the price that product had in that store that week. The result for
the chosen slice is saved as one parquet file that later steps read.

## The raw files (fingerprinted)

The sha256 fingerprint of each file is stored in `config/raw_files.yaml`; every run stops if a file
has changed.

| File | Data rows | Size | sha256 (start) |
|---|---|---|---|
| calendar.csv | 1,969 | 0.1 MB | `d12b5914ef03e666...` |
| sell_prices.csv | 6,841,121 | 203.4 MB | `9da3ad1f8b8ccacd...` |
| sales_train_evaluation.csv | 30,490 | 121.7 MB | `4b4a47c44c38380d...` |

The calendar has 1,969 days, more than the 1,941 days of sales: the extra days were the
competition's future test period and simply do not join to any sales row.

## Choosing the slice

All of M5 is 30,490 series x 1,941 days = 59,181,090 rows, likely too much for an 8 GB laptop
once features are added. Options:

| State | Category | Series | Stores | Items | Rows (series x days) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| CA | FOODS | 5,748 | 4 | 1,437 | 11,156,868 |
| CA | HOBBIES | 2,260 | 4 | 565 | 4,386,660 |
| CA | HOUSEHOLD | 4,188 | 4 | 1,047 | 8,128,908 |
| TX | FOODS | 4,311 | 3 | 1,437 | 8,367,651 |
| TX | HOBBIES | 1,695 | 3 | 565 | 3,289,995 |
| TX | HOUSEHOLD | 3,141 | 3 | 1,047 | 6,096,681 |
| WI | FOODS | 4,311 | 3 | 1,437 | 8,367,651 |
| WI | HOBBIES | 1,695 | 3 | 565 | 3,289,995 |
| WI | HOUSEHOLD | 3,141 | 3 | 1,047 | 6,096,681 |

Chosen (in `config/scope.yaml`, with the reason): **CA / FOODS**: 5,748 series,
11,156,868 rows, 2011-01-29 to 2016-05-22 (1,941 days).

| Store | Series | Units sold |
|---|---|---|
| CA_1 | 1,437 | 5,471,661 |
| CA_2 | 1,437 | 3,567,477 |
| CA_3 | 1,437 | 7,625,660 |
| CA_4 | 1,437 | 2,871,065 |

| Department | Series | Units sold |
|---|---|---|
| FOODS_1 | 864 | 2,410,777 |
| FOODS_2 | 1,592 | 3,018,605 |
| FOODS_3 | 3,292 | 14,106,481 |

Memory: the parquet file is about 13 MB on disk. Loaded into pandas with the text columns
stored as categories, it needs about 80 bytes per row, about 0.89 GB in total
(estimated from a 200,000-row sample). That fits an 8 GB laptop; later steps should still load only
the columns they need.

## Checks on the prepared slice

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| Duplicate product-store-day rows | 0 |
| Duplicate (store, item, week) keys in the price file | 0 |
| Missing or negative unit values | 0 / 0 |
| Rows with no calendar date | 0 |
| Days with zero sales | 60.1% of all rows; 48.2% of days the item was on sale |
| Days with no price (item not on sale that week) | 2,572,521 rows (23.1%) |
| ...of which after the item's first listed week (gaps) | 0 rows in 0 series |
| Series never listed at all | 0 |
| Sales on days with no price | 0 |
| Total units sold | 19,535,863 |
| Rows on a SNAP day | 33.0% |
| Rows on a named event day | 8.1% |

"No price" means the product was not on sale in that store that week. There are no sales on any
of those days, which supports reading them as "not on the shelf" rather than "nobody wanted it".
So later steps will leave them out of training and scoring instead of counting them as zero demand.
Even on days the item was on sale, about half the days have zero sales: much of this demand is
intermittent, which F2 measures per series.

## The holdout is reserved now

The last 28 days, d_1914 to d_1941 (2016-04-25 to 2016-05-22), are the final
holdout. F1 only prepares them; nothing is fitted or tuned on them until the one holdout run in F4.

## How to reproduce

1. Download the M5 data from Kaggle (account + accepting the competition rules) and put
   `sales_train_evaluation.csv`, `calendar.csv` and `sell_prices.csv` in `data/raw/`.
2. `python -m venv .venv && .venv/bin/pip install -r requirements.txt && .venv/bin/pip install -e .`
3. `.venv/bin/python -m forecast.run_f1` (checks fingerprints, builds `data/processed/m5_slice.parquet`)
4. `.venv/bin/python -m pytest` (unit tests) and `.venv/bin/python -m pytest -m realdata`
